business: NuViewer 0.4.1 (free Windows image viewer / gallery / editor suite)
target: Windows 10/11 desktop users who open pictures every week and already have a viewer they use (Windows Photos, IrfanView, XnView MP, FastStone, ImageGlass, Honeyview, nomacs, or none)

segments.name: Digital artist / designer / illustrator (PSD, AI, PNG, alpha)
3D / game / VFX artist (TGA, DDS, EXR, HDR, GLB, OBJ, FBX)
Office / general home user (phone photos, screenshots, PDF)
Power user / IT / developer (keyboard-driven, lightweight, tinkerer)
Collector / archivist / manga-comic reader (huge folders, zips, cbz)

current_apps.name: Windows Photos (built in)
current_apps.how: Never changed the default; it opens when you double-click a picture.

current_apps.name: IrfanView
current_apps.how: Installed years ago, knows its shortcuts, has the plug-ins set up.

current_apps.name: XnView MP / XnView
current_apps.how: Uses it as a browser plus batch converter and metadata tool.

current_apps.name: FastStone Image Viewer
current_apps.how: Uses its full-screen mode, browser and simple editor daily.

current_apps.name: ImageGlass
current_apps.how: Chose it for the modern look and open-source licence.

current_apps.name: Honeyview / Bandiview / qView / nomacs / PicView (other fast viewer)
current_apps.how: Picked a small fast viewer; happy but not attached.

current_apps.name: Adobe Bridge / Lightroom / Photoshop used as the viewer
current_apps.how: Opens heavy Adobe apps just to look at a file, hates the wait, keeps the catalogue there.

current_apps.name: Explorer thumbnails + whatever app opens (no viewer chosen)
current_apps.how: Does not think about viewers; browses in Explorer.

current_apps.name: Specialist tools (Blender, Honeyview for comics, MPC-HC/VLC for video, RawTherapee/darktable)
current_apps.how: Uses a different app per file type.

behaviours.name: Speed-obsessed
behaviours.how: Notices every 200 ms delay; will switch for speed alone.

behaviours.name: Set-and-forget loyalist
behaviours.how: Changed viewers once years ago, has muscle memory, hates relearning.

behaviours.name: Format-hunter
behaviours.how: Switches the moment an app opens a file type the old one fails on.

behaviours.name: Trust / security cautious
behaviours.how: Won't install unknown .exe from a solo dev without reviews, source or signing.

behaviours.name: Feature maximalist
behaviours.how: Likes one app that does view, edit, batch, convert.

behaviours.name: Minimalist
behaviours.how: Wants a viewer that does only viewing and stays out of the way.

behaviours.name: Early adopter / tries every new tool
behaviours.how: Installs new tools on a whim, posts about them.

behaviours.name: Workflow-locked pro
behaviours.how: Pipeline depends on catalogue/XMP/plugins/colour setup that cannot break.

objections: Another image viewer? Mine already works fine.
One developer, version 0.4: will it still be maintained next year?
Is an unknown .exe safe? Is it signed? Is it open source?
I would have to relearn shortcuts and reset my file associations.
Does it open MY files (my RAW camera, my plugin formats) correctly?
Windows only, no portable-everything story I rely on (or I also use Mac/Linux).
The speed difference is a few tens of milliseconds, I would not feel it.
It does too much (gallery, editor, importer, tray agent) and I only want a viewer.
My colour management / catalogue / XMP workflow must not change.
No plugins, no big community, hard to find help.
habits: you open pictures from Explorer by double-click dozens of times a day
you cull a card of 500 RAW+JPG photos after every shoot
you flip through hundreds of screenshots and PNG exports from your work
you open phone photos your relatives sent you and want to print one
you read manga or comics from zip/cbz files
you check texture, HDR and 3D model files from your game project
you have a hard drive with 200,000 pictures from the last 15 years
you reinstall Windows every year or two and keep a list of apps
